description: MARIDA is the Marine Debris Archive published by Kikaki and collaborators for detecting marine debris and other sea-surface features in Sentinel-2 imagery. The dataset contains 1,381 patches of 256 by 256 pixels, with class masks, annotator-confidence masks, georeferenced shapefiles and train-validation-test splits. Fifteen classes distinguish debris from water, ships, vegetation, foam, clouds and related features. Coverage consists of selected dated satellite tiles, not a continuous global survey. Public data are free under CC-BY-4.0, verified through DataCite; the GitHub repository documents access and baseline workflows. A limitation is weak supervision and varying annotation confidence, so class masks should not be treated as uniformly certain observations. The baseline environment also specifies older Python and machine-learning dependencies. MARIDA can calibrate marine-waste detection for cleanup and coastal-infrastructure simulations, complementary to Delft3D FM (model-delft3d-fm) for transport calculations. Its 2022 PLOS ONE paper describes the benchmark. No image patches, shapefiles or baseline model files were downloaded.
